evals.prompt: We've got a folder of 40 loose requirements organized as 'high-level' and 'detailed'. Help me restructure this into a proper spec.
evals.expected_output: Recommends reorganizing around business events instead of the high/low split, proposes the three-area structure (Problem / Solution / Business Events), and asks which decomposition hierarchy (use-case track vs. story track) the project wants to standardize on.

evals.prompt: Some of our requirements have an ID, description, and priority; others just have a description. What schema should every requirement record have?
evals.expected_output: Proposes one consistent schema (Number, Description, Rationale, Type, Fit Criterion, Source, Satisfaction/Dissatisfaction, Conflicting/Dependent Requirements, Supporting Material, Version Number) applied to every requirement regardless of type, and flags missing IDs as a hard gate to fix immediately.

evals.prompt: Write a goal statement for this project: "reduce cart abandonment."
evals.expected_output: Produces Purpose/Advantage/Measurement structure, explicitly calling out that the Measurement line is what makes the goal later verifiable, not just aspirational.
